# PennyLane API Reference {#sec-api-reference}

Quick reference for the PennyLane APIs used in this book. See the official
documentation at <https://docs.pennylane.ai> for full details.

## Devices

```python
qml.device("default.qubit",    wires=n)   # Pure Python simulator
qml.device("lightning.qubit",  wires=n)   # C++ simulator (fast)
qml.device("lightning.gpu",    wires=n)   # GPU simulator (requires CUDA)
```

## QNode Decorator

```python
@qml.qnode(dev, diff_method='adjoint')    # fastest for most circuits
@qml.qnode(dev, diff_method='parameter-shift')  # required for reuploading
@qml.qnode(dev, interface='torch')        # enables PyTorch autograd
```

| `diff_method` | Speed | Supports reuploading |
|--------------|-------|----------------------|
| `'adjoint'` | Fast | No |
| `'parameter-shift'` | Slow (2 evals/param) | Yes |
| `'backprop'` | Fast (requires `default.qubit`) | Yes |

## Single-Qubit Gates

| Gate | PennyLane | Matrix |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Pauli-X (NOT) | `qml.PauliX(wire)` | $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ |
| Pauli-Y | `qml.PauliY(wire)` | $\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$ |
| Pauli-Z | `qml.PauliZ(wire)` | $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ |
| Hadamard | `qml.Hadamard(wire)` | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ |
| $R_X(\theta)$ | `qml.RX(theta, wire)` | $e^{-i\theta X/2}$ |
| $R_Y(\theta)$ | `qml.RY(theta, wire)` | $e^{-i\theta Y/2}$ |
| $R_Z(\theta)$ | `qml.RZ(theta, wire)` | $e^{-i\theta Z/2}$ |

## Two-Qubit Gates

```python
qml.CNOT(wires=[control, target])
qml.CZ(wires=[control, target])
qml.SWAP(wires=[wire0, wire1])
qml.CRY(theta, wires=[control, target])
qml.CSWAP(wires=[control, wire0, wire1])   # Fredkin gate
```

## Data Encoding

```python
qml.AngleEmbedding(features, wires, rotation='Y')
# features: (n_qubits,) — one angle per qubit

qml.AmplitudeEmbedding(features, wires, normalize=True)
# features: (2^n_qubits,) — full amplitude vector

qml.BasisEmbedding(features, wires)
# features: binary list/array of length n_qubits
```

## Ansatz Templates

```python
qml.BasicEntanglerLayers(weights, wires, rotation=qml.RY)
# weights shape: (n_layers, n_wires)

qml.StronglyEntanglingLayers(weights, wires)
# weights shape: (n_layers, n_wires, 3)
```

## Measurements

```python
qml.probs(wires)          # probability vector, shape (2^n,)
qml.expval(observable)    # scalar ∈ [-1, +1]
qml.state()               # full statevector, shape (2^n,)
qml.sample(observable)    # raw samples
```

Common observables:
```python
qml.PauliZ(wire)
qml.PauliX(wire)
qml.Hermitian(matrix, wires)
```

## Visualisation

```python
print(qml.draw(circuit)(args))          # ASCII diagram
qml.draw_mpl(circuit)(args)             # matplotlib figure
qml.draw_mpl(circuit, decimals=2)(args) # rounded parameter values
```

## Differentiation

```python
# Gradient of scalar-output circuit
grad_fn = qml.grad(circuit)
grads   = grad_fn(params, x)

# Jacobian for vector-output circuit
jac = qml.jacobian(circuit)(params)

# Adjoint of a unitary template
qml.adjoint(qml.StronglyEntanglingLayers)(weights, wires=wires)
```

## PyTorch Integration

```python
# 1. QNode with torch interface
@qml.qnode(dev, interface="torch", diff_method="adjoint")
def circuit(inputs, weights):
    ...

# 2. Wrap as nn.Module layer
weight_shapes = {"weights": (n_layers, n_qubits, 3)}
layer = qml.qnn.TorchLayer(circuit, weight_shapes)

# 3. Use in nn.Module
class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.q = layer
        self.out = nn.Linear(1, 1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.out(self.q(x).float().unsqueeze(-1))
```

## Native Optimisers (PennyLane only)

```python
opt = qml.AdamOptimizer(stepsize=0.05)
opt = qml.GradientDescentOptimizer(stepsize=0.01)
opt = qml.RMSPropOptimizer(stepsize=0.01)
opt = qml.NesterovMomentumOptimizer(stepsize=0.01, momentum=0.9)

# One step
params = opt.step(cost_fn, params)

# One step + cost value
params, cost_val = opt.step_and_cost(cost_fn, params)
```
